channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold edges lower as firmer US Dollar caps recovery
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges lower on Monday as a firmer US Dollar (USD) and mild profit-taking cap gains following last week's rebound from a more than seven-month low of $3,941.

item.title: Euro: Range-bound against US Dollar under Fed support – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner says EUR/USD is consolidating above 1.1400 as markets reassess European Central Bank (ECB) and Fed paths, with a September ECB hike priced below 50% probability.

item.title: 162.30: Japanese Yen falls back to near 40-year lows as intervention risks loom
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) has resumed its broader downtrend against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday following a mild relief last week.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness and intervention risks persist against US Dollar – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists argue that the USD/JPY pair is trading near its highest level in around 40 years and may have shifted into a new, higher range.

item.title: WTI Oil falls as oversupply concerns outweigh recent rebound
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil trades around $68.30 at the time of writing on Monday, down 0.64% on the day, as investors continue to assess the global supply outlook following the latest production decisions by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies (OPEC+).

item.title: Euro remains depressed against British Pound despite positive Eurozone data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains depressed near one-year lows against the British Pound (GBP) on Monday, hitting session lows below 0.8560 after pulling back from Friday’s highs at 0.8575.

item.title: Euro: Choppy range outlook against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley notes that EUR/USD recently fell below its prior 1‑month forecast of 1.15, prompting a reassessment of projections.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD struggles to extend recovery above 20-day EMA
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) is down 0.8% to near $4,140 during the European trading session on Monday. The precious metal faces selling pressure as the three-day rally hits a pause after failing to extend above $4,202.

item.title: British Pound: Sterling strength on positioning and flows – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes that Sterling has been the strongest G10 currency since the Makerfield by-election, helped by a still-sizeable but reduced speculative short base.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Aiming for the 0.8065 area amid wide US Dollar strength
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) pares recent gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, as fresh frictions in the Middle East are dampening investors’ appetite for risk in an otherwise calm market session.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar declines on weaker commodity prices, RBNZ policy uncertainty
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5680 at the time of writing, down 0.50% on the day as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under pressure against a stronger US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy risks support higher yields – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that the Japanese Yen (JPY) has weakened again, pushing USD/JPY back above 162.00 and coinciding with further selling at the long end of the JGB curve.

item.title: Indian Rupee declines against US Dollar, lower oil prices to limit downside
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD) at the start of the week.

item.title: CEE FX: Dovish signals challenge gains – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky notes weaker US data and a softer Dollar helped Central and Eastern European (CEE) currencies, but focus now shifts to local inflation and central banks.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $62.02 per troy ounce, down 0.64% from the $62.42 it cost on Friday.

item.title: Euro: Fiscal questions with disinflation progress – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that European disinflation is allowing focus to shift from emergency inflation control toward growth and fiscal credibility.

item.title: Euro holds gains against Japanese Yen following Eurozone Retail Sales
item.description: EUR/JPY continues to gain ground for the second successive day, trading around 185.30 during the European hours on Monday. The currency cross remains stronger as the Euro (EUR) holds ground following the release of key economic data from the Eurozone and Germany.

item.title: Oil: Supply rebound and glut concerns – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Henry Hao and Charlie Lay highlight a structural shift in Oil as a US–Iran interim peace deal boosts crude supply and restores shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Seven OPEC+ members will lift output again in August, raising fears of a global crude glut.

item.title: United States Dollar Index (DXY) Price Forecast: Retakes 101.00 amid bullish setup
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, regains positive traction at the start of a new week and, for now, seems to have snapped a two-day losing streak.

item.title: Eurozone Retail Sales rises 0.2% MoM in May, misses 0.3% estimates
item.description: Eurozone Retail Sales rise at a moderate pace of 0.2% Month-on-Month (MoM) in May against the estimates of 0.3%. In April, Retail Sales, a key measure of consumer spending, declined by 0.4%.

item.title: Japanese Yen: New lows risk against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note USD/JPY has pulled back after testing resistance near 162.80 but is still holding above the March peak around 160.40.

item.title: Euro drifts lower as investors’ cautiousness offsets upbeat German factory data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) shows a moderately negative stance against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, in a calm start of the week.

item.title: Canadian: Business Outlook Survey to gauge confidence with energy shock – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economists Nathan Janzen and Abbey Xu note the Bank of Canada’s (BoC) Q2 Business Outlook Survey will show how firms reacted to recent energy price volatility, with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) previously near US$100.

item.title: Dow Jones futures advance ahead of ISM Services PMI
item.description: The Dow Jones futures gain 0.18% to trade above 53,280, while S&P 500 futures rise 0.46%, trading near 7,560. Meanwhile, Nasdaq 100 futures advance 1.03% to trade near 29,860 during European trading hours on Monday.

item.title: Euro: Upside bias capped by nearby resistance against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang highlights that EUR/USD remains in a short-term range, with flat momentum indicators pointing to intraday consolidation between 1.1415 and 1.1455.

item.title: Gold hangs near daily low as Hormuz risks support USD; receding Fed hike bets limit losses
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) recovers slightly from the daily low, albeit it retains the negative bias through the first half of the European session and remains below a two-week high touched earlier this Monday.

item.title: US Dollar: Services data guide Fed expectations – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that softer U.S. labor data and easing inflation have reduced pressure for further Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening, but upcoming US Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) and ISM Services will be crucial for rate expectations.

item.title: Australian Dollar drifts away from highs amid cooler inflation, weak employment data
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is trading moderately lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, as cooler Australian inflation figures have eased pressure on the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to hike interest rates further.

item.title: British Pound rallies back closer to multi-year top as carry trade and fiscal woes hit JPY
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross gains strong follow-through positive traction for the second successive day and rallies to mid-216.00s during the early European session on Monday, back closer to a multi-year peak set in late April.

item.title: British Pound: Sterling gains against Euro face political test – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner highlights a sizeable downside breakout in EUR/GBP driven by stale Sterling shorts and lower FX volatility reducing appetite to pay carry.
